To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synchronization of activity in locust groups arises from an entrained physiological rhythm, and is mediated by the distribution of food resources.
the synchronization of activity in locust groups is mediated by the distribution of food and that this is achieved through the entrainment of internal rhythms.

synchronization of physiological rhythms and behaviour in locusts is driven by entrainment of the individual's internal rhythms by the activity of neighbours, and that resource distribution mediates the coupling between individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how resource distribution mediates the synchronization of physiological rhythms and behaviour in groups of animals.
how the distribution of resources mediates the synchronization of physiological rhythms, and thus behaviour, in animal groups.
the role of internal physiological rhythms in the emergence of synchronized behaviour in animal groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distribution of food resources in the environment determines the coupling between individuals in a group.
synchronization is a function of resource distribution and the strength of the coupling between individuals.
the spatial distribution and density of resources mediate the coupling between individuals and the synchronization of their physiological rhythms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resource distribution mediates synchronization in locust groups.
synchronization in animal groups is mediated by resource distribution and the strength of coupling among individuals.
the spatial distribution and availability of resources in a group of animals determines the strength of coupling of individuals and the degree of synchronization of their behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synchronization in animal groups can be understood in terms of the distribution of resources and the entrainment of individual rhythms.
resource distribution can control coupling between individuals, and this coupling can mediate the synchronization of behaviour in groups.
the spatial distribution and density of resources can affect the synchronization of activity in animal groups.
